newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH FOREST OWNERS WANT WOOD PRICE HIKES.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH FOREST OWNERS WANT WOOD PRICE HIKES.

text.p: Finnish forest owners want higher wood prices in talks starting next Monday to cover higher costs caused by a new law that requires softer forestry methods, a forest owner representative said on Friday.
"We will see 100 to 200 million markka in additional costs due to the new forest legislation," Timo Kalli told Reuters. He declined to give any exact price target for the talks.

Kalli chairs a committee appointed by the Central Union of Agricultural Producers and Forest Owners (MTK) to represent the forest owners in 1997 wood price talks with Finland biggest forest industry group UPM-Kymmene Oy .

Kalli said trade would slow down unless the talks are completed successfully by the end of March but he did not expect the new company specific wood price talk system to make talks any easier than earlier talks. "The system is unclear," he said.

Current wood prices are based on the previous regional agreement which expired at the end of December but according to the Finnish Forest Research Insitute's (METLA) statistics, they have been rising since July last year.
